Below is the shortest, repeatable path to:

1. Run the Vicuña model (either 7 B or 13 B parameters) on your own GPU
2. Talk to it through LangChain

The instructions are split into two parts:

• Part A – get Vicuña running locally (fastchat)
• Part B – wrap Vicuña in LangChain so you can use it just like any other LLM in LangChain

Pick your hardware tier and follow the matching steps.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
PART A – Install & run Vicuña locally
--------------------------------------------------------------------
You have three practical ways to run Vicuña today:

- Option 1 – 1-click with Oobabooga text-generation-webui (easiest, Windows + Linux)
- Option 2 – FastChat CLI (minimal, Linux/WSL only)
- Option 3 – vLLM (multi-GPU & 4-bit quantized, fastest on A100/H100)

OPTION 1 – Oobabooga (GUI, Windows + Linux)
--------------------------------------------
1. Clone repo
   ```
   git clone https://github.com/oobabooga/text-generation-webui
   cd text-generation-webui
   ```
2. Install (Python 3.10-3.11)
   ```
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```
3. Download Vicuña 7B model
   ```
   python download-model.py lmsys/vicuna-7b-v1.5
   ```
4. Launch web UI
   ```
   python server.py --model lmsys_vicuna-7b-v1-5
   ```
   The model will be available at http://localhost:7860.

OPTION 2 – FastChat (CLI, Linux/WSL, 1 GPU)
--------------------------------------------
FastChat is the original repo that served Vicuña; it is still the cleanest single-GPU way.

1. Clone
   ```
   git clone https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat
   cd FastChat
   ```
2. Make a fresh venv (Python 3.9-3.11)
   ```
   python -m venv venv
   source venv/bin/activate   # or .\venv\Scripts\activate on Windows
   ```
3. Install
   ```
   pip install fschat
   ```
4. Pull Vicuña 7B (or 13 B) from hugging-face.
   Vicuña weights are gated; you need to:

   • Accept the model license on HuggingFace:
     https://huggingface.co/lmsys/vicuna-7b-v1.5
   • Create a token with **read** access (Settings → Access Tokens)
   • Export the token once:
     ```
     export HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=hf_xxxxxxxxxxx
     ```

5. Download the model
   ```
   python -m fastchat.model.download_model --model-name lmsys/vicuna-7b-v1.5
   ```
6. Start the worker
   ```
   python -m fastchat.serve.cli --model-path ./models/vicuna-7b-v1.5
   ```
   The worker starts a local API at http://localhost:21000.

OPTION 3 – vLLM (multi-GPU or 4-bit, fastest)
--------------------------------------------
vLLM can run Vicuña 13 B in 4-bit on a single 24 GB GPU or split across 2×A100.

1. Clone
   ```
   git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm
   cd vllm
   ```
2. Install
   ```
   pip install -e .
   ```
3. Serve Vicuña 13 B 4-bit
   ```
   python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
     --model lmsys/vicuna-13b-v1.5 \
     --dtype float16 \
     --quantization bitsandbytes
   ```
   This starts an Open-AI compatible server at http://0.0.0.0:8000.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
PART B – Integrate with LangChain
--------------------------------------------------------------------
LangChain speaks three “flavors” of local LLMs:

• HuggingFacePipeline (for HuggingFace Transformers `pipeline`)
• LLMLocal (for Oobabooga / Kobold / Exllamav2)
• OpenAI (for vLLM & FastChat that expose `/v1/chat/completions`)

Below are the minimal snippets for each path.

----------------------------------------
1. Using Oobabooga (LLMLocal)
----------------------------------------
Install LangChain + the local wrapper:

```
pip install langchain langchain-community
```

Python snippet:

```python
from langchain_community.llms import OobaboogaLLM

llm = OobaboogaLLM(
    model="lmsys_vicuna-7b-v1-5",
    base_url="http://localhost:7860",  # change port if you changed it
    temperature=0.7,
    max_new_tokens=512,
)

from langchain import PromptTemplate, LLMChain
prompt = PromptTemplate.from_template("Q: {question}\n A:")
chain = LLMChain(llm=llm, prompt=prompt)
print(chain.run("What is 2+2?"))
```

----------------------------------------
2. Using FastChat API (OpenAI flavor)
----------------------------------------
FastChat worker already exposes `/v1/chat/completions`.
Tell LangChain to talk OpenAI style:

```python
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

llm = ChatOpenAI(
    openai_api_key="dummy",          # not used
    openai_api_base="http://localhost:21000/v1",
    model_name="vicuna-7b-v1.5",
    temperature=0.7,
)
```

Then use it like any ChatOpenAI model.

----------------------------------------
3. Using vLLM OpenAI Server
----------------------------------------
Same snippet as FastChat; vLLM uses the same endpoint.

```python
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
llm = ChatOpenAI(
    openai_api_key="dummy",
    openai_api_base="http://localhost:8000/v1",
    model_name="vicuna-13b-v1.5",
)
```

----------------------------------------
4. Using Transformers pipeline (CPU / single GPU)
----------------------------------------
If you insist on running straight Transformers without FastChat / vLLM:

```python
from langchain_community.llms import HuggingFacePipeline
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, pipeline
import torch

model_id = "lmsys/vicuna-7b-v1.5"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_id,
    device_map="auto",
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,
    trust_remote_code=True,
)

pipe = pipeline(
    "text-generation",
    model=model,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    max_new_tokens=512,
    temperature=0.7,
)

llm = HuggingFacePipeline(pipeline=pipe)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
Troubleshooting checklist
--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. CUDA / cuDNN versions match your PyTorch wheel.
2. Vicuña is a **gated** model -> you must have accepted its terms on HuggingFace and exported `HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN`.
3. Oobabooga needs ~14 GB VRAM for 7 B, 28 GB for 13 B.
4. If you get `OutOfMemory`, load 4-bit:
   `--load-8bit` (Oobabooga) or `--quantization bitsandbytes` (vLLM).
5. LangChain OpenAI wrapper: you can omit `openai_api_key` but must leave it non-None; use `"dummy"` as shown above.

That’s it—you now have Vicuña + LangChain up and running locally.
